supporting_from: For m>=3 and the simple Cayley graph of C_2*C_m with S={a,b,b^-1}, h_E>=1-2/m>0, p_u=1, and p_c is the unique p in (0,1) solving p[2 sum_{k=1}^{m-1}p^k-(m-1)p^m]=1.
supporting_to: For independent Bernoulli(p) bond percolation, n pairwise edge-disjoint finite x-y cutsets F_i imply P_p(x connected to y) <= product_i[1-(1-p)^|F_i|].
rationale: L4's bridge cuts satisfy L1's disjoint edge-index hypothesis; L2 then excludes uniqueness.

supporting_from: The independent barrier-exploration attempt does not prove pc<pu for a general one-ended nonamenable Cayley graph. A fresh effective-barrier construction or quantitative nonmerger bound at some p>pc is still required.
supporting_to: For a connected locally finite one-ended graph with maximum degree d and edge Cheeger constant h_E>0, the number of disjoint x-y cuts of size at most K is at most d(|B_R(x)|+|B_R(y)|), R=ceil(K/h_E)+1. This is uniform in x,y on vertex-transitive graphs.
rationale: L3 gives a uniform finite bound on size-K cut multiplicity; the parent lane lacks a fresh-barrier replacement.

supporting_from: For an infinite connected d-regular vertex-transitive undirected graph and normalized walk operator P=A/d with rho=||P||_2, pd rho<1 implies tau_p(x,y)<=(pd rho)^dist(x,y)/(1-pd rho), so pu>=1/(d rho). Thus pc<1/(d rho) suffices for pc<pu, without being necessary.
rationale: Scoped correction only: the prior concept says 'p_c < 1/rho (Benjamini-Schramm criterion)' with normalized rho. L5 proves the degree-scaled sufficient bound, while pc<=1<1/rho makes the prior reduction vacuous. No refutation of the parent conjecture.
